front.title: Telemetry Methodologies for Analog Measurement Instrumentation

abstract.t:
Evolution toward network operations automation requires systems encompassing software-based analytics and decision-making. Network- based instrumentation provides crucial data for these components and processes. However, the proliferation of such instrumentation and the need to migrate the data it generates from the physical network to "off-the-network" software poses challenges. In particular, analog measurement instrumentation, which generates time-continuous real-number data, may generate significant data volumes.
This document discusses methodologies for handling analog measurement instrumentation data, informed by the requirements of network digital twins and of automated fault diagnosis. It proposes that instrumentation report, for each measured quantity and each interval, a summary that keeps the level, the rate of change, the departure from a steady trend, the extremes over a stated short window and the number of measurements taken. Such summaries can be combined exactly over any longer span, and they allow trends, brief events and stopped measurements to be detected and reported as they occur.
